h1: A lawn, pet area or putting green on your Foxfield acreage.
lede: Choose a useful outdoor area near the house while keeping the rest of the property working. Start with a free site visit and written estimate.
wins: Keep wells, septic and access in the plan
Separate a dog area from other animal use
Use available room for putting and chipping

answer.question: How should turf be planned around a Foxfield well and septic system?
answer.answer: Bring the recorded locations and any applicable requirements for those systems before placing the turf area. Obtain suitable guidance before proposing preparation over or near a septic component. Keep access available, and account for any cleaning water the chosen turf use will need.

blocks.h2: Give dogs a defined area beside the larger property.
paras: A pet area near the door can be separate from drives, paddocks and a practice green. Plan the route your dogs use, cleanup access and the edge where turf meets the rest of the ground. Do not assume pet turf is intended for every animal or paddock use.
For golf, use the available room for purposeful putts and a chipping position. Leave room for routine property access rather than spreading the green across a route you still need.

blocks.h2: Locate the systems beneath the land.
paras: Show us well and septic records, known utilities and any existing drainage features. Ask the appropriate authority or system professional about proposed work nearby. A large lot does not make every open area available for excavation or compaction.

Foxfield has Town requirements for grading and lot coverage. Ask how they apply to the whole proposal and bring the response to the estimate. If you rely on a well, check its permitted use when planning cleaning and the planting that will remain.

servicesNote: Compare a lawn near the house, a dedicated dog area and a practice green around the property’s existing uses.
